s6-middle-of-a-linkedlist-tortoisehare-m.trick: Move slow one node and fast two nodes at a time. Slow finishes at the middle (the second middle when the length is even).

s6-reverse-a-linkedlist-iterative.trick: Save the next node before redirecting the current link backward. The previous pointer becomes the new head.

s6-reverse-a-ll-recursive.trick: Reverse the suffix first, then make its original first node point back to the current node.

s6-detect-a-loop-in-ll.trick: Floyd's two pointers move at different speeds. They meet if and only if the list contains a cycle.

s6-find-the-starting-point-in-ll.trick: After the two pointers meet inside a cycle, move one to the head. Walking both one node at a time finds the cycle entry.

s6-length-of-loop-in-ll.trick: Once Floyd's pointers meet, walk around the cycle until returning to that node and count the links.

s6-check-if-ll-is-palindrome-or-not.trick: Find the first half's end, reverse the second half, compare values, then reverse it back to restore the list.

s6-segrregate-odd-and-even-nodes-in-ll.trick: Separate nodes by 1-based position, not by value. Keep odd and even chains, then append the even chain.

s6-remove-nth-node-from-the-back-of-the-.trick: Keep fast n nodes ahead of slow, starting from a dummy node. When fast reaches the last node, slow precedes the target.

s6-delete-the-middle-node-of-ll.trick: Slow moves one node while fast moves two. Retain the predecessor of slow so the middle can be unlinked.

s6-sort-ll.trick: Merge sort fits linked lists: split with slow/fast pointers, sort both halves, then merge by relinking nodes.

s6-find-the-intersection-point-of-y-ll.trick: Walk pointers from both heads; when a pointer reaches the end, restart it at the other head. They cover equal total distance and meet at the shared node.

s6-add-1-to-a-number-represented-by-ll.trick: For digits stored most-significant first, recurse to the tail with carry 1. Propagate the carry backward and prepend a 1 if needed.

s6-add-2-numbers-in-ll.trick: For digits stored least-significant first, add corresponding digits and carry, building the answer from the units place onward.

s6-delete-all-occurrences-of-a-key-in-dl.trick: For every matching node, reconnect its existing neighbors, update the head if needed, and delete the detached node.

s6-find-pairs-with-given-sum-in-dll.trick: The doubly linked list must be sorted. Start at both ends and move inward according to the sum, just like two pointers on a sorted array.

s6-remove-duplicates-from-sorted-dll.trick: Because equal values are adjacent in a sorted list, compare each node with its successor and unlink duplicates in place.

s6-reverse-ll-in-group-of-given-size-k.trick: Reverse exactly k nodes at a time. First check that a full group exists; leave a shorter final group unchanged.

s6-introduction-to-linkedlist-learn-abou.trick: A singly linked node stores a value and a pointer to the next node. The head points to the first node; nullptr marks the end.

s6-inserting-a-node-in-linkedlist.trick: To insert at a 0-based position, find the preceding node and link the new node between it and its former successor. Position 0 updates the head.

s6-deleting-a-node-in-linkedlist.trick: To delete at a 0-based position, find its predecessor, bypass the target, and release it. A dummy head also handles position 0.

s6-find-the-length-of-the-linkedlist-lea.trick: Follow next pointers from the head until nullptr, counting one node per step.

s6-search-an-element-in-the-ll.trick: Traverse the list and compare each node's value with the target; stop at the first match.

s6-introduction-to-dll-learn-about-struc.trick: A doubly linked node stores both next and prev pointers. Set both directions whenever linking adjacent nodes.

s6-insert-a-node-in-dll.trick: Insert at a 0-based position by connecting the new node to its two neighbors and updating both neighbors' pointers.

s6-delete-a-node-in-dll.trick: Find the node at a 0-based position, reconnect its previous and next neighbors, then delete it.

s6-reverse-a-dll.trick: Swap each node's prev and next pointers; the last node processed becomes the new head.

s6-sort-a-ll-of-0-s-1-s-and-2-s-by-chang.trick: Partition nodes into three chains for 0, 1 and 2, then join those chains. This relinks nodes without changing their values.

s6-rotate-a-ll.trick: Reduce k modulo the length. Connect tail to head to make a ring, then cut after length-k nodes for a right rotation.

s6-flattening-of-ll.trick: Each top-level node starts a sorted bottom chain. Merge all chains with a min-heap, joining the result through bottom pointers.
s6-flattening-of-ll.time: O(N log k), N total nodes and k chains

s6-clone-a-linked-list-with-random-and-n.trick: Interleave each clone after its original, assign clone random pointers via original->random->next, then separate the two lists.
